summary:
Antigua and Barbuda requires real caution. On 5 July 2022, in Orden David et al v The Attorney General of Antigua and Barbuda, the Eastern Caribbean Supreme Court declared Sections 12 and 15 of the Sexual Offences Act 1995 unconstitutional and void, decriminalising consensual same-sex intimacy between adults. Before that ruling, adult-on-adult buggery carried up to fifteen years' imprisonment, five years where a minor committed the act, and life where an adult committed it against a minor; 'serious indecency' carried up to ten years where the target was a child under sixteen, and people convicted of buggery as repeat offenders were placed on the Sex Offenders Register for life.

The same ruling read the constitutional prohibition on sex discrimination to cover sexual orientation and gender identity. That interpretive holding does not amount to a statutory protection regime. Antiguan law does not address discrimination or harassment on account of sexual orientation or gender identity, so a visitor refused service, housing or transport on these grounds has no statute to invoke, only the constitutional argument the court opened in 2022.

Same-sex unions are not recognised in any form, and households headed by same-sex couples are not eligible for the same rights given to opposite-sex married couples. There is no mechanism to change a legal gender marker; only name changes are available. Outright International records that transgender people are particularly vulnerable as a result.

Official hostility predates the ruling. At the May 2016 Universal Periodic Review, Argentina, Australia, France, Germany, the Netherlands and Nicaragua all urged the government to repeal its sodomy ban and guarantee full human rights to LGBTQ people. Minister of Social Transformation Samantha Marshall called the ban antiquated and said it should be repealed, while Parliamentary Secretary Maureen Payne-Hyman assured the Council that LGBTQ people are not persecuted in the country. On 24 August 2016 the government announced it had no intention of repealing the ban, while acknowledging that a lawsuit would most certainly strike it down given the identical jurisprudence in Belize.

Physical violence against LGBTQ people has been documented. Orden David, the Antiguan activist who challenged the anti-sodomy law and won in 2022, was bullied and physically attacked, struck in the head and knocked out in daylight. The Eastern Caribbean Alliance for Diversity and Equality announced in December 2019 that it would file a legal challenge by the end of that year, arguing that buggery and indecency laws stigmatise and legitimise hate speech, discrimination and violence; the challenge covered Barbados, St Kitts-Nevis, Antigua and Barbuda, Grenada and Saint Lucia, and culminated in the 2022 ruling. Six Caribbean countries still criminalise same-sex conduct.

The Advocates for Human Rights' January 2025 submission to the UN Human Rights Committee lists LGBTQ+ rights issues for Antigua and Barbuda ahead of its review, documenting the open SOGI-protection questions the state still faces post-2022 decriminalisation.
tangentialFactors:
The 2022 decriminalisation sits within a wider Caribbean pattern: six countries in the region still criminalise same-sex conduct, and the Eastern Caribbean Alliance for Diversity and Equality pursued parallel challenges in Barbados, St Kitts-Nevis, Grenada and Saint Lucia alongside Antigua and Barbuda. A visitor moving between islands should not assume the Antiguan ruling travels with them.

The gap between the court's constitutional reading and the absence of statute is the central turbulence in Antiguan and Barbudan LGBTQ law. The constitutional argument is available but untested as a tool against private actors such as landlords, employers or carriers, and no anti-discrimination body exists to hear such complaints.
localsOnly:
Residents can change their name but have no legal route to change a gender marker on official documents, which leaves transgender Antiguans and Barbudans without matching identification. Same-sex households are excluded from the rights attached to opposite-sex marriage, including inheritance, next-of-kin and social-protection entitlements.

Repeat buggery convictions before July 2022 placed offenders on the Sex Offenders Register for life; the status of people already on that register following decriminalisation is not addressed in the sources. Antiguan law contains no provisions on discrimination or harassment based on sexual orientation or gender identity, so residents have no administrative complaint mechanism.
outOfScopeNotes: Whether the 2022 ruling has been appealed, legislatively回应 or incorporated into a revised Sexual Offences Act is not sourced here. The practical enforcement record of the constitutional anti-discrimination reading since 2022 is also unresolved in the inventory. Sources do not address gender-affirming healthcare access, prison placement policy for transgender detainees, or whether Antigua and Barbuda has any legal framework for asylum or refugee protection on SOGI grounds.
